message.content:
Below is everything you’ll need to pull the **graph‑IDs** that contain the IP `145.34.45.56` from VirusTotal’s v3 Graphs API: | Step | What to Do | |------|------------| | **1️⃣ Build the URL** | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/graphs/ip/145.34.45.56?limit=8&cursor=cursor_b` | | **2️⃣ Set up authentication** | Add an `Authorization` header with your bearer token (`api_key_2`). Example:
`Authorization: Bearer api_key_2` | | **3️⃣ Make the request** | You can hit the endpoint with cURL, Postman, or any HTTP client. Below is a ready‑to‑run cURL snippet: | ```bash curl -X GET \ "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/graphs/ip/145.34.45.56?limit=8&cursor=cursor_b" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "x-apikey: api_key_2" ``` > *Note:* > • Replace `api_key_2` with the actual API key value. > • If you’re using the newer “Bearer” scheme instead of `x-apikey`, change the header to: `-H "Authorization: Bearer "`. --- ### 📥 Expected Response Structure A successful call returns something like: ```json { "data": [ { "id": "graph_id_123", ... }, { "id": "graph_id_456", ... } /* …up to 8 items */ ], "meta": { ... } // pagination info, timestamps, etc. } ``` To extract just the list of IDs, run a quick jq filter (or equivalent): ```bash ... | jq '.data[].id' ``` That will print each ID on its own line. --- #### Quick recap * **Endpoint:** `/api/v3/graphs/ip/` * **Query params:** `limit=8 & cursor=cursor_b` * **Auth header:** `x-apikey: api_key_2` *(or `Authorization: Bearer …`)* * **Result extraction:** Pull `.data[*].id`. Once you’ve executed the above, you’ll have all eight graph identifiers that reference the target IP. Happy hunting!
